pages.text: Rotation taught me to think in motion. Now I wanted something that could travel: lightning, tamed into copper wire, flowing wherever I strung it.
I raised my first multiblocks with a hammer: coke ovens, blast furnaces, steel. A windmill on a dynamo gave me my first flux, and I sat beside the capacitor watching the number climb.
Then the chests went away. Everything I owned became light inside a crystal network, and I could ask it for anything. Air, squeezed hard enough, did the rest of the work.
Deep underground I found oil, black and patient. Some nights, I admit, I read the darker books and called the spirits that answer them. They work hard, and they never complain.
Four million flux, filled by my own generators. Proof that my power no longer flickered.
pages.title: Mark of the Industrial Age
